newsitem.title: USA: Nebraska voters shoot down tax limit measure.
newsitem.headline: Nebraska voters shoot down tax limit measure.

text.p: A proposed constitutional amendment to limit total operating property taxes for local governments in Nebraska was heartily defeated Tuesday by voters.
The Nebraska Secretary of State's office reported 74 percent of voters rejected the measure.

A companion proposed amendment to include quality education as a fundamental right and direct the legislature to create a new funding system also went down in defeat, with 77 percent of voters saying no, the office reported.

The two constitutional amendments had been placed on the ballot as a result of a successful petition drive. A third proposed amendment, that would have eliminated property taxes beginning in January 1998, failed to be certified for the ballot.

In an unsuccessful effort to head off the petition drives to lower taxes, the Nebraska Legislature passed in April a two percent cap on local government budget increases in fiscal 1997 and a limit on their property tax levies starting in 1999.
Moody's Investors Service Inc and Standard & Poor's Corp said they were concerned about the effect of the proposed amendments on local governments.

Nebraska voters also rejected a proposed amendment allowing the legislature to authorize off-track paramutuel betting on horses, and another proposed amendment that would have allowed the merger of local governments with voter approval, according to the secretary of state's office.
